title: Development of 3D Printed Flow Cells for Correlative Imaging Pipelines: From Live Cell Imaging Under Flow to Frozen-Hydrated Cryo-EM
content: 3D printing has revolutionized various engineering, biomedical, and biophysical research processes. From rapid prototyping to use as a manufacturing tool, 3D printing has become an essential technology for many sectors. Within the wide range of use cases, 3D printing has become valuable for creating channeled flow cell devices used in cellular biology, microbiology, and structural biology [1]. Additive manufacturing processes can rapidly create high-resolution components or entire devices from a range of material feedstocks, allowing for multiple iterations of a design to be created, printed, tested, and revised over a 24-hour period. These capabilities have expanded the scope of our research surrounding the creation and integration of flow cells in correlative microscopy pipelines.
